question_text: A physician at an internal medicine ward notices that several of his patients have hyponatremia without any associated symptoms. Severe hyponatremia, often defined as < 120 mEq/L, is associated with altered mental status, coma, and seizures, and warrants treatment with hypertonic saline. Because some patients are chronically hyponatremic, with serum levels < 120 mEq/L, but remain asymptomatic, the physician is considering decreasing the cutoff for severe hyponatremia to < 115 mEq/L. Changing the cutoff to < 115 mEq/L would affect the validity of serum sodium in predicting severe hyponatremia requiring hypertonic saline in which of the following ways?
